lessons.title: Arrays & Vectors
lessons.html:
Linear Data Structures

Understand memory layout and performance characteristics of arrays vs dynamic arrays.

Fixed Array vs Vec:

// Fixed size array [T; N] - stack allocated
let arr: [i32; 5] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
assert_eq!(arr[2], 3);

// Dynamic Vec<T> - heap allocated
let mut vec = Vec::new();
vec.push(10);
vec.push(20);
vec[0] = 100; // Direct indexing

// Capacity & Reserve
vec.reserve(10); // Pre-allocate space

Performance:

OperationArrayVec
AccessO(1)O(1)
Insert End-Amortized O(1)
Insert Middle-O(n)

lessons.title: Linked Lists
lessons.html:
Custom Linked List Implementation

Master pointers, ownership, and recursive data structures.

Node & List:

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Node<T> {
    value: T,
    next: Option<Box<Node<T>>>,
}
impl<T> Node<T> {
    fn new(value: T) -> Self {
        Node { value, next: None }
    }

    fn push(&mut self, value: T) {
        let new_node = Box::new(Node::new(value));
        new_node.next = self.next.take();
        self.next = Some(new_node);
    }
}

lessons.title: Binary Search Trees
lessons.html:
Balanced BST Implementation

Self-balancing trees for O(log n) operations.

AVL Tree Node:

#[derive(Debug)]
struct AVLNode<T> {
    value: T,
    height: usize,
    left: Option<Box<AVLNode<T>>>,
    right: Option<Box<AVLNode<T>>>,
}
impl<T: Ord> AVLNode<T> {
    fn insert(&mut self, value: T) -> bool {
        if value < self.value {
            if let Some(ref mut left) = self.left {
                left.insert(value)
            } else {
                self.left = Some(Box::new(AVLNode::new(value)));
                true
            }
        } else if value > self.value {
            // Similar for right
        }
        self.rebalance();
        false // Already exists
    }
}

lessons.title: Hash Tables
lessons.html:
Rust HashMap Internals

Understand hashing, collisions, and load factors.

Custom HashMap:

use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
use std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher;

struct MyHashMap<K, V> {
    buckets: Vec<Vec<(K, V)>>,
    size: usize,
}
impl<K: Hash + Eq, V> MyHashMap<K, V> {
    fn insert(&mut self, key: K, value: V) {
        let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();
        key.hash(&mut hasher);
        let hash = hasher.finish() as usize % self.buckets.len();
        self.buckets[hash].push((key, value));
    }
}

lessons.title: Graphs & BFS/DFS
lessons.html:
Graph Algorithms

Breadth-first and depth-first traversal with applications.

Adjacency List:

use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque, HashSet};

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct Graph<T> {
    adj: HashMap<T, Vec<T>>,
}
impl<T: Eq + Hash + Clone> Graph<T> {
    fn bfs(&self, start: &T) -> Vec<T> {
        let mut visited = HashSet::new();
        let mut queue = VecDeque::new();
        queue.push_back(start.clone());
        
        while let Some(node) = queue.pop_front() {
            if !visited.insert(node.clone()) { continue; }
            for neighbor in self.adj.get(&node).unwrap() {
                queue.push_back(neighbor.clone());
            }
        }
        visited.into_iter().collect()
    }
}

lessons.title: Sorting Algorithms
lessons.html:
Master O(n log n) Sorting

Implement QuickSort, MergeSort, and compare performance.

QuickSort (In-place):

fn quicksort<T: PartialOrd>(arr: &mut [T]) {
    if arr.len() <= 1 { return; }
    
    let pivot_idx = partition(arr);
    quicksort(&mut arr[0..pivot_idx]);
    quicksort(&mut arr[pivot_idx + 1..arr.len()]);
}

lessons.title: Dynamic Programming
lessons.html:
Optimize with Memoization

Solve complex problems by breaking into subproblems.

Fibonacci DP:

fn fib_memo(n: usize, memo: &mut HashMap<usize, u64>) -> u64 {
    if let Some(&result) = memo.get(&n) {
        return result;
    }
    
    let result = if n <= 1 { n as u64 } else {
        fib_memo(n - 1, memo) + fib_memo(n - 2, memo)
    };
    
    memo.insert(n, result);
    result
}
